title: perf(console): move the `types` zod validators off the eager budgeted line
body:
Fixes #10065

Clause-②: no — no `packages/*/src` published source moved. `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` exits 0 and prints *"No source or published contract of a released package changed in this range, so no changeset is owed"*. ⚠️ Stated as the gate's verdict rather than copied from a claim: this card carried no claim comment to copy the line from.

## The defect

`advancedChunks`'s `framework` group claims every `packages/types/` module **wherever it is reached from**, and that chunk is eager because `core` and `react` are reached from the entry. So the nine `packages/types/src/zod/**` validator modules rode the **eager, budgeted** line although their only live consumer in the console bundle is `packages/plugin-map/src/ObjectMap.tsx` — which imports `ObjectMapConfigSchema` from `@object-ui/types/zod` and sits behind a lazy boundary. Every page load fetched validators only the object-map view reads.

Same defect class as objectui#9345, one tier over: a grouping rule deciding membership independently of reachability.

## The premise, re-derived on this branch's own base (`0c2eb5eee`)

Probe and must-miss control, one command, over every emitted chunk:

| probe | leg BEFORE (`0c2eb5eee`) | leg AFTER (`46083d761`) |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `.describe('ObjectQL object name')` from `objectql.zod.ts` | `assets/framework-C1GNpb8T.js` | `assets/types-zod-DUmm1NEb.js` |
| control: `.describe('Action execution mode for chaining')` from `crud.zod.ts` | absent from every chunk | absent from every chunk |
| `plugin-map` chunk in the eager closure? | no (absent from the 329-chunk eager list) | no |
| `plugin-map` chunk statically imports the validators' chunk? | through `framework` | `from"./types-zod-DUmm1NEb.js"` |

The composition, read from the build's own visualizer on the BEFORE leg: the nine modules are **140,541 rendered bytes** of a **372,430-byte** `framework` chunk, led by `objectql.zod.ts`, `data-display.zod.ts` and `complex.zod.ts`.

⚠️ **One card figure did not reproduce, and it is worth saying plainly.** The card's *"27.6% of the eager `framework` chunk"* was measured on objectui#9488's branch, where `framework` held 162 modules / 509,658 rendered bytes. On `origin/main` that chunk holds 108 modules / 372,430 rendered, so the same nine modules are **37.7%** of it. The membership claim reproduced exactly; the share is leg-dependent and the card's number belongs to the other leg.

## ⭐ What only the counterfactual could show: a SECOND consumer, created by the fix itself

The first counterfactual build **failed**, and it failed for a reason no source-level search can reach. Rolldown's `CodeSplittingGroup.includeDependenciesRecursively` **defaults to `true`**, so the new group captured the nine validators *and recursively absorbed* three shared modules — `packages/types/src/data-display.ts`, `complex.ts`, `designer.ts`. The **eager** `plugin-grid` chunk reads runtime values out of those (`ObjectGrid.tsx` imports `normalizeTableColumnType` and `isSystemManagedField` from `@object-ui/types`), and rolldown removes a higher-priority group's modules from the lower-priority ones, so `framework` never got them back. `plugin-grid` then had to import the new chunk statically and **all 140,541 bytes stayed eager** — a saving of exactly nothing, dressed as a new chunk name.

The guard printed it, naming both the co-tenant chunk and the source edge:

```text
[assert-types-zod-stays-lazy] the `@object-ui/types/zod` validators are back in the EAGER closure ...
  assets/types-zod-BBjRnjYY.js — statically imported by assets/plugin-grid-CB5tL5XA.js
      packages/types/src/data-display.ts  <-  packages/types/src/index.ts
      packages/types/src/complex.ts       <-  packages/types/src/index.ts
      packages/types/src/designer.ts      <-  packages/types/src/index.ts
```

The repair is `includeDependenciesRecursively: false` on that one group, which is also what the group MEANS: the validators are what has no eager reader, not everything they happen to import. Their non-zod dependencies fall back to `framework`, where they were and where they belong.

## Measurement — both legs, one container, one command family

Per leg: `pnpm exec turbo run build --filter='./packages/*' --concurrency=2`, then `pnpm --filter @object-ui/console build`, then `node scripts/check-eager-closure-budget.mjs`. Exit codes captured by redirect-then-read, never across a pipe. ⛔ No ceiling, baseline, allowance or floor constant was touched — `MAX_EAGER_CLOSURE_GZIP_BYTES`, `PER_CHUNK_GZIP_CEILINGS`, `PER_CHUNK_BASELINE`, `EXHAUSTED_HEADROOM_ALLOWANCES` and `EXHAUSTED_HEADROOM_FLOOR_MULTIPLE` are byte-identical on both legs.

| reading | BEFORE `0c2eb5eee` | AFTER `46083d761` | delta |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|
| `framework` gzipped | 69,560 | **41,782** | **-27,778** |
| `framework` raw | 244,780 | 129,863 | -114,917 |
| `framework` headroom vs its unchanged 100,000 ceiling | 30,440 (0.3340x) | 58,218 (0.6388x) | |
| **whole eager closure** gzipped | 3,132,117 | **3,104,341** | **-27,776** |
| whole eager closure raw | 10,604,860 | 10,489,968 | -114,892 |
| eager chunks / total | 329 / 2309 | 329 / 2310 | 0 / +1 |
| `pnpm check:eager-closure` exit | 0 | **0** | |

⭐ **The eager chunk COUNT is unchanged and the total is one higher** — the bytes *left* the closure into a new lazy chunk rather than moving to another eager line. `ui-components` (+8), `data-adapter` (+7) and `plugin-grid` (-21) are the only other rows that moved at all; that is import bookkeeping, and it is why the whole-closure delta (-27,776) and the `framework` delta (-27,778) agree to 2 bytes.

### The saving against the card's bracket — it lands OUTSIDE it, above

The card priced the shrink as a bracket, **20,695 – 26,322 gzipped**, deliberately not a point estimate, because nobody had built the counterfactual. This branch is the counterfactual.

**The real figure is 27,778 gzipped — 1,456 bytes ABOVE the top of the bracket (5.5% over).** Reported as a finding, not as a win: both estimators were computed against objectui#9488's `framework` leg (95,454 gz over 509,658 rendered), and the share they divided by is the 27.6% that does not hold on `main`. The bracket's *ranking* conclusion survives — the saving clears the 0.10x floor's 4,568-byte requirement by 6.1x — but its *endpoints* were anchored to the other leg and the top one is not an upper bound.

## What this does and does not do for objectui#9488

It restores headroom on the row that PR's `Bundle Analysis` job exits 2 about. It does **not** land that PR, and it is not measured against it: this branch is based on `origin/main`, and the two have not been built together. ⚠️ One interaction the reviewer should know about, stated rather than left to be discovered: objectui#9488 adds a chunk-membership half that asserts `packages/types` lands **wholly** in `framework`. After this change `packages/types` is deliberately split across `framework` and `types-zod`, so whichever lands second owes that assertion an update. Nothing here touches that PR.

## The guard, and why it checks REACHABILITY first

`scripts/vite-types-zod-lazy.ts` runs in `generateBundle` on every console build — CI and local — and refuses a build in **both** directions:

1. **The validators are no longer reachable from `plugin-map`.** This is the failure that *looks like a saving*: if they are dropped from the graph (a `sideEffects` declaration that shakes too hard, an import narrowed to `import type`, a group whose test stops matching), the eager closure gets smaller, every byte ceiling goes greener, and the object-map view throws at runtime for a schema that is not in the bundle. No byte ceiling can tell a deferral from a deletion. This one can, so it is reported first — an author told "the bundle grew" deletes more.
2. **The validators are back in the eager closure.** Loud anyway, but the budget answers *how many bytes* and never *which boundary broke*; this names the importing chunk and, through the module graph, the importing source module.

Three counter-probes fail **closed** before either verdict: no chunk holds a validator module, no chunk holds a `plugin-map` module, or the eager walk cannot see `react-dom`. Both verdicts are negative, so a matcher that matched nothing would agree with a correct bundle on both.

## Ablation ledger — red before, green after, restores verified

Every leg: mutate, prove on disk that the mutation landed (`grep -c` of the removed text, expected 0), run, restore with `git checkout HEAD -- PATH`, prove `git diff HEAD` is empty. All four restores verified clean.

| leg | mutation | what reds | result |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 | drop `includeDependenciesRecursively: false` from the group | `keeps the group from absorbing its own dependencies` | exit 1, 1 failed / 14 passed |
| 2 | drop `viteTypesZodLazy()` from the plugins array | `registers the guard, or nothing weighs the bundle at all` | exit 1, 1 failed / 14 passed |
| 3 | tie the group's priority to `framework`'s 80 | `routes the zod validators ... at a priority framework cannot tie` + `leaves no second claimant` | exit 1, 2 failed / 145 passed |
| 4 | narrow the group parser's tail back to a closing brace | `finds the whole group table, not a fragment of it` + the routing case | exit 1, 2 failed / 145 passed |

Leg 4 is the reason `scripts/__tests__/check-eager-closure-budget.test.ts` is in this diff at all. That file's `parseGroups` required `priority` to be the group's **last** property, and the new group carries an option after it — so the group was silently absent from the attribution table while every case below went on passing. Measured before the widening: 42 groups parsed, `types-zod` not among them. That is the parse's own *"a matcher that matches nothing agrees with everything"* note firing on itself.

And the bundle-level half this change still gets for free: the first counterfactual build above is the guard's real red leg, on the real graph, with the real cause named.

## Verification run

| check | exit | note |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `pnpm exec turbo run build --filter='./packages/*'` | 0 | 39/39, on the final head |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/console build` | 0 | guard prints *lazy and still reachable ... all reached from 1 `@object-ui/plugin-map` chunk(s)* |
| `node scripts/check-eager-closure-budget.mjs` | 0 | table above |
| `node scripts/check-eager-locale-catalogues.mjs` | 0 | `en` resident, 9 catalogues deferred — unchanged |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` | 0 | no changeset owed |
| `pnpm type-check:scripts` | 0 | |
| `pnpm check:unreferenced-sources` | 0 | |
| `pnpm check:control-bytes` | 0 | 8118 tracked text files |
| `pnpm check:new-line-citations` | 0 | 0 new citations |
| `pnpm check:test-path-roots` | 0 | |
| `pnpm lint:root` | 0 | 32 warnings, 0 errors, none in the four changed files |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/console lint` | 0 | 212 warnings, 0 errors, none in the changed file |
| `pnpm exec vitest run scripts/` | 0 | 176 files / 5259 tests passed, 2 skipped |

**NOT MEASURED**, declared rather than skipped silently: `pnpm check:docs-route-closure` — it weighs `apps/site`'s own route closure and needs that app's build; nothing in this diff reaches it. And the object-map view was verified **structurally** (the emitted `plugin-map` chunk carries `from"./types-zod-DUmm1NEb.js"`, and the `ObjectQL object name` literal resolves inside that chunk) rather than in a browser.

## Out of scope, named rather than taken

- `PER_CHUNK_GZIP_CEILINGS.framework` now stands 58,218 bytes (0.64x the 89 KiB regression) above the live measurement, up from 0.33x. Re-pinning it **down** is the honest follow-up and would restore the row's resolution — but a ceiling edit is exactly what this card was forbidden to make, and it is a deliberate re-pin for the seat, not an in-lane change.
- `PER_CHUNK_BASELINE.framework` (72,245) is now far above the measurement it is compared against by hand. That constant is a historical reading anchored to its own build and is not read by the sensitivity leg, so it is stated, not moved.
